katie (devex): Heads up — the new generator sample in onboarding leaks a goroutine if you don't explicitly cancel the ctx. saw it in the sample app when I left a stream open :grimacing:

mike (go-sdk): ugh. can you paste the snippet? we tried to make the iterator simple for newbies, maybe we missed the cancel semantics

katie (devex): sure. minimal repro from the sample app:```goctx := context.Background()it := client.Generator(ctx, req)defer it.Close()for it.Next() { fmt.Println(it.Token()) } // if caller forgets to cancel/Close, runtime still spins```

devon (eng): that Close() call is subtle. in typical go iter patterns Close() is optional, or at least documented. new users just use Background and expect GC to handle it :/

mike (go-sdk): right — our current design passes the ctx into the runtime and the SDK spawns a goroutine to pump tokens. If caller uses context.Background() and never Close()/cancel, our pump waits on network read and never returns; ctx isn't tied to caller lifecycle.

sam (platform): Is this auth-related at all? I've seen streams hang when token refresh happens mid-stream and the handshake retries silently

katie (devex): yes, saw that too. sequence: initial token ok -> mid-stream auth-refresh triggered -> runtime does a transparent reconnect -> our iterator's internal state doesn't handle the reconnect path and blocks Next().

mike (go-sdk): ok -> two problems: (1) ergonomic ownership of cancellation, (2) reconnect path leaking Next() blocked goroutine. Proposed quick fixes: make the generator require an explicit context (not Background) and add an ergonomic helper that returns a cancel func, plus document it in onboarding; and fix reconnect to surface an error on the iterator so Next() returns false and Err() shows cause.

devon (eng): API suggestion: change signature to Generator(ctx context.Context, req ... ) GeneratorIterator where the iterator does NOT spawn internal goroutines unless ctx is cancellable. For onboarding, provide a helper: NewGeneratorWithCancel := func(req) (it, cancel) that does context.WithCancel internally and wires Close() to cancel.

katie (devex): love the helper. most sample-app users copy-paste, so having a single-liner that 'just works' prevents a lot of flakes in smoke tests and examples. also update README with an explicit pattern: use ctx from main or signal handler.

mike (go-sdk): implementation note: we also need to ensure Close() is idempotent and that Next() returns after Close() even if reads are blocked. I'll add a small select with a done chan that Close closes.

sam (platform): for auth-reconnect, propose we add a visible state transition event to the iterator: it.OnEvent(func(e Event){ if e.Type==AuthRefreshed { log } }) — but maybe that's heavy. Alternatively: set iterator.Err() to a wrapped ErrAuthRefreshOnReconnect so callers can differentiate transient vs fatal.

devon (eng): +1 for specific Err types. Many customers build retry layers assuming stream is stable and silently swallowing; explicit Err makes debugging easier.

katie (devex): can we ship a docs blurb and a tiny sample patch as a quick follow-up? I'll open the onboarding PR with the helper and a note in the quickstart about cancellation patterns.

mike (go-sdk): I'll own the SDK change. Plan: (A) make Close() cancel the internal ctx and close done channel (B) ensure Next() unblocks and returns false with Err set (C) add NewGeneratorWithCancel helper and update sample-app commit. ETA: end of week if no surprises.

devon (eng): ping CI bot for flaky test that covers forgetting cancel. also add unit test that simulates mid-stream auth refresh and asserts Next() returns error instead of blocking.

ci-bot: queued job 7623: gen-iter-leak-repro-test — running

katie (devex): one more micro-ux ask: in the sample app we currently show a for it.Next() loop with no timeout. Could we show a pattern using context.WithTimeout or wiring main signal handling example? New devs copy that straight into prod.

mike (go-sdk): yes, I'll update the sample to use:```goctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)defer cancel()it := client.NewGeneratorWithCancel(ctx, req)defer it.Close()for it.Next() { fmt.Print(it.Token()) }if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Fatalf("stream error: %v", err) }```

devon (eng): feel free to drop a short note in the release notes — "Go SDK: improved generator cancellation semantics & helper" — so that teams see the behavior change.

katie (devex): thanks everyone. I'll add a tiny onboarding paragraph about "when to use WithCancel/WithTimeout vs passing top-level ctx" and link to the sample. :sparkles:

mike (go-sdk): thanks — will update the PR link when CI passes. tagging @devex for follow-up docs review.
